issues.legal_issue: The urgency procedure may be used to acquire land for house sites for poor people and dispense with an opportunity to object when the government considers immediate possession necessary.
material_facts: The land was acquired for allotment of house sites to poor people.
The State invoked the urgency procedure and dispensed with the objection inquiry.
The State amendment expressly covered acquisition for dwelling houses for the poor and related housing purposes.
issues.conclusion: Dispensing with the objection inquiry was lawful in these circumstances.
issues.legal_principle: The Punjab amendments to the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, including Section 17(2)(b), authorized the urgency power under Section 17(4) to be used for the specified public purposes, including dwelling houses for the poor, with the result that the inquiry under Section 5-A could be dispensed with. Applying Chameli Singh v. State of U.P., which considered the earlier reasoning in Naryan Govind Gavate v. State of Maharashtra, providing house sites to poor people is an urgent necessity and dispensing with the inquiry is justified where the government considers immediate possession necessary.

predicates.challenge_to_compulsory_acquisition: A party challenged a compulsory land acquisition that used an urgency procedure.
predicates.acquisition_for_house_sites_for_poor_peo: The land was acquired to provide house sites for poor people.
predicates.government_considered_immediate_possessi: The government considered immediate possession of the land necessary.

issues.definition: When a compulsory acquisition challenged by a party is for house sites for poor people and the government considered immediate possession necessary, dispensing with the objection inquiry is lawful.

issues.legal_issue: Taking possession through the accepted formal process completes a compulsory acquisition even if the former owner remains physically on the land and compensation remains to be determined.
material_facts: The acquisition award was made and possession was taken after the challenge to dispossession was dismissed.
The land was earmarked and distributed to landless workers after possession was taken.
The former owner claimed it had retained physical possession.
Compensation had been deposited, and the Court stated that compensation determination was what remained after the acquisition process was completed.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition was final after possession was taken, and the former owner's continued occupation did not invalidate it; only compensation remained to be determined.
issues.legal_principle: The accepted mode of taking possession in compulsory acquisition is to prepare a Panchnama in the presence of witnesses, take possession, and deliver it to the beneficiaries. Retention of the land thereafter amounts to unlawful possession and does not undo the acquisition. Once possession has been taken, the acquisition process is complete, although compensation may remain to be determined.

predicates.challenge_to_compulsory_acquisition: A party challenged a compulsory land acquisition.
predicates.possession_taken_through_accepted_formal: The acquiring authority took possession through the accepted formal process and delivered the land to the beneficiaries.
predicates.former_owner_remained_in_occupation: The former owner continued to occupy the land after possession had been taken.

issues.definition: When a challenged compulsory acquisition is followed by possession through the accepted formal process, the acquisition remains final even if the former owner continues to occupy the land.

issues.legal_issue: A former owner need not be given a further opportunity to ask the government to use other land or leave the acquired land out of the acquisition after the acquisition process is complete.
material_facts: The appellant asked for an opportunity to make a representation to the State Government.
The acquisition process had already been completed by the taking of possession.
The appellant owned substantial other land and was not thereby prevented from continuing its proposed educational activity.
issues.conclusion: No further opportunity to make a representation was required.
issues.legal_principle: Where the acquisition process has already been completed, the Court need not give the former owner liberty to seek a discretionary change from the government; the appellant's ownership of other land also meant the acquisition did not disable its proposed educational activity.

predicates.challenge_to_compulsory_acquisition: A party challenged a compulsory land acquisition.
predicates.acquisition_process_completed: The acquisition process had been completed, including the taking of possession.
predicates.former_owner_has_other_suitable_land: The former owner has other land and is not thereby prevented from pursuing the activity for which it sought the acquired land.

issues.definition: When a challenged compulsory acquisition is complete and the former owner has other land that leaves its proposed activity possible, no further opportunity to seek a change from the government is required.
